Inglewood, California
  July 9, 2019

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  July 9, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.
  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
  hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts/Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  and Franklin; and
  Absent:  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing
  Authority Member Morales.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Franklin, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated June
  27, 2019, in the amount of $3,894,277.24, and dated July 5, 2019, in the amount of
  $1,389,572.57 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Franklin and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member
  Morales.

131.8  PUBLIC HEARING CONTINUED – FICAL YEAR 2019-2020 ANNUAL ACTION
  PLAN - CONTINUED. Public hearing to receive public comments on the Fiscal Year
  2019-2020 Annual Action Plan.

  Public hearing continued to July 16, 2019 at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

  1
 July 9, 2019

  132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending denial
  of the following claims:

  a) James Catron for alleged property damage on May 12, 2019.
  b) Diane Lee for alleged property damage on July 21, 2018.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  and carried that the above listed claims be denied.

 125  AGREEMENT NO. 19-234 APPROVED – ADMINSURE, INC. Staff report dated
  July 9, 2019, was presented recommending approval of a five (5) year cooperative
  purchase agreement with AdminSure, Inc., to provide liability claims management
  services, per the terms and conditions of their agreement with Newport Beach.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 19-234 in the total amount of
  $939,666.07. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

 101  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 19-051 APPROVED – CYPRESS
  PRIVATE SECURITY, LP. Staff report dated July 9, 2019, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 19-051 with Cypress
  Private Security, LP, to reflect a company name change of Universal Protection Service
  LP, dba Allied Universal Security Service.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 19-051.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

 178  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 18-244 APPROVED –
  CALIFORNIA HIGHWAY PATROL. Staff report dated July 9, 2019, was presented
  recommending approval of an amendment to Agreement No. 18-244 with California
  Highway Patrol (CHP) for usage of the Inglewood Police Department’s Shooting Range.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve the amendment to do the following: 1)
  Establish a flat monthly usage rate of $2,083; and 2) Extend the term of the agreement to
  June 30, 2022. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

 183  AGREEMENT NO 19-235 APPROVED – FLEETWASH INC. Staff report dated
  July 9, 2019, was presented recommending approval of a three-year agreement (with the
  option to extend two (2) additional three (3) year terms) with FleetWash Inc., for pressure
  washing services, and bus stop maintenance.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 19-235 in the annual amount
  of $160,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

  2
 July 9, 2019

 131.8  AGREEMENT NO. 19-236 APPROVED – HABITAT FOR HUMANITY OF
  GREATER LOS ANGELES; CDBG MINOR HOME REHABILITATION
  PROGRAM GUIDELINES APPROVED; RESOLUTION NO. 19-81 ADOPTED –
  AMENDING THE 2018-2019 FISCAL YEAR BUDGET. Staff report dated July 9,
  2019, was presented recommending approval of an agreement with Habitat for Humanity
  of Greater Los Angeles for administration and construction services related to the City’s
  Minor Home Rehabilitation Program.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby:1) Approve Agreement No. 19-236 in an amount of up
  to $500,000; 2) Approve the CDBG Minor Home Rehabilitation Program Guidelines; and
  3) Adopt Resolution No. 19-81 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR
  2018-2019 BUDGET RELATING TO CONSOLIDATED PLAN GRANT
  FUNDS AND THE MINOR HOME REHABILITATION PROGRAM

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

  David Esparza, Assistant City Manager/CFO introduced the new Housing Manager, Mr.
  Robert Chavez.

 142  ORDINANCE NO. 19-14 INTRODUCED AND ADOPTED – APPROVED
  SECURED PROPERTY TAX RATE FOR THE FISCAL YEAR BEGINNING
  OCTOBER 1, 2019. Staff report dated July 9, 2019, was presented recommending the
  introduction and adoption of an ordinance approving the secured property tax rates for
  Fiscal Year beginning October 1, 2019.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Mayor Butts that further
  reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

  Thereupon, the City Clerk read the title of Ordinance No. 19-14 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWQOOD, CALIFORNIA,
  AUTHORIZING THE LEVY AND COLLECTION OF A PROPERTY
  TAX ON TAXABLE PROPERTY IN THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  FOR PARTIAL FUNDING OF THE INGLEWOOD FIRE AND POLICE
  RETIREMENT SYSTEM AND THE INGLEWOOD CITY
  EMPLOYEES’ RETIREMENT SYSTEM FOR THE FISCAL YEAR
  BEGINNING OCTOBER 1, 2019

  was introduced by Council Member Franklin.

  Furthermore, it was moved by Mayor Butts and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that Ordinance No. 19-14 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA,
  AUTHORIZING THE LEVY AND COLLECTION OF A PROPERTY
  TAX ON TAXABLE PROPERTY IN THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  FOR PARTIAL FUNDING OF THE INGLEWOOD FIRE AND
  POLICE RETIREMENT SYSTEM AND THE INGLEWOOD CITY
  EMPLOYEES’ RETIREMENT SYSTEM FOR THE FISCAL YEAR
  BEGINNING OCTOBER 1, 2019

  3
 July 9, 2019

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.

 219  REPORTS – CITY TREASURER. Wanda Brown, City Treasurer, mentioned the
  Bonds and C.D.’s she purchased on behalf of the City, and gave a brief report on local
  and state news.

 127.1  COUNCIL INITIATIVE:

  Council Member Dotson:

  Initiative by Council Member George W. Dotson requesting approval of the City’s in-
  kind co-sponsorship of the 1st Annual District 1 City of Champions 5K Run/Walk, to be
  held on Saturday, September 28, 2019, from 7:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., at Edward Vincent
  Park.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Franklin that the City
  Council does hereby approve co-sponsorship in an amount not to exceed $1,000. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Morales.
  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.
  Willie Agee commented that he supports CI-1, initiative by Council Member George W.
  Dotson requesting approval of the City’s in-kind co-sponsorship of the 1st Annual District
  1 City of Champions 5K Run/Walk, and encouraged everyone to come out September 28,
  2019, and be a part of this wonderful event.

  Cinder Eller, invited everyone to come out on Saturday, July 13, 2019, to have coffee
  with a cop on Oak and Manchester.

  (No name given), stated people should be allowed to enter the City Hall building on the
  2nd floor. He also commented that there is an issue in the city with a lot of stray dogs,
  and criminals in the City of Inglewood.

  Ray Davis, 2nd District, stated the activities on the 4th of July were more civilized than
  other years.

  Michael Benbow commented that he does not like that fireworks are allowed in the City
  of Inglewood.

  Erick Holly invited everyone to attend the Inglewood Chamber of Commerce golf
  tournament on July 26, 2019. He stated folks can contact the Chambers office for more
  information.

  Robert Pullen Miles, District Director for Assembly Woman Autumn Burke, invited the
  residents of the 62nd Assembly District to her Back to School Health and Wellness event
  happening at Crozier Middle School 120 W. Regent Street, Inglewood, CA, on August 3,
  2019, from 10:00 a.m. until 3:00 p.m.

  4
 July 9, 2019

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in memory of Tyler Skaggs at the hour of 2:40 p.m.

  Approved this 13th day of August, 2019

  _________________________
  Yvonne Horton, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
